headline: Genomic sequence models extended to single-cell, individual and generative outputs
label: Genomic Foundation Model Adaptation
summary: Sequence and genotype models are now being adapted to predict single-cell and individual-level genomic readouts rather than bulk population averages.
synthesis: The dominant thread is extending sequence-to-function and pretrained genomic models toward cell-type-specific and individual-specific readouts. Scooby-2 fine-tunes AlphaGenome with a cell-specific decoder to predict single-cell RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility tracks from DNA sequence. TFXcan combines Enpact, which pairs Enformer with IMPACT, with genotypes to predict personalized TF binding and links TF-tissue pairs to prostate cancer risk loci. UniLoopNet extends sequence-based prediction to multi-task chromatin interaction classes. MMRL applies self-supervised representation learning to somatic missense mutations across ~50,000 tumors, outperforming TMB for prognosis. SPARK differs methodologically, inferring enhancer-gene regulatory networks through Bayesian structure learning from single-cell multiome data and prior knowledge. What is new is the move toward single-cell and individual-level outputs; the items do not share a common benchmark.
